sections.h2: What should a Jefferson County homeowner know about the county itself?
sections.html:
Jefferson County is the most populous county in Alabama and the central county of the Birmingham-Hoover metro area. It had 674,721 residents in 2020, and the Census estimate for 2025 is 665,742.

The county stretches over roughly 1,124 square miles of ridge and valley country, which makes it the fifth largest in Alabama by land area. It was established in 1819, and its first seats were Carrollsville and then Elyton, which served until 1873. The county's long history of iron, coal and limestone mining and steelmaking explains why so many neighborhoods began as company or industrial towns.

sections.h2: Which cities and areas make up Jefferson County?
sections.html:
The county holds dozens of municipalities and unincorporated communities. The larger cities include Birmingham, Bessemer, Hoover, Homewood, Vestavia Hills, Mountain Brook, Trussville, Gardendale, Hueytown, Pleasant Grove, Center Point and Fultondale.

Some of them straddle county lines. Birmingham, Hoover, Vestavia Hills, Helena, Leeds and Trussville each reach partly into another county, and Sumiton and Warrior do the same. If your house is in one of those places, the county that bills the tax depends on where the parcel sits, not on the city name in the mailing address.

Several former towns, including Ensley, North Birmingham, Woodlawn and Elyton, are now Birmingham neighborhoods. Their housing stock is often older, and long-owned family homes there change hands through estates more often than newer subdivisions do.

sections.h2: What are the Jefferson County property tax dates?
sections.html:
The Alabama Department of Revenue states that property taxes are due October 1 and delinquent after December 31. That schedule applies in Jefferson County as it does across the state.

The state timetable that follows runs like this:

  • October 1: taxes due.
  • January 1: taxes delinquent.
  • February: delinquent accounts turned over to the probate court.
  • March: the probate court meets.
  • April: parcels advertised for sale.
  • May: tax sale.

A bill covers the previous tax year, so a payment made in the fall is for the year that ended the prior September 30, according to how the neighboring Lauderdale County office explains the cycle. If you sell in the middle of the year, the closing agent splits the tax between buyer and seller.

sections.h2: How does Alabama classify and value a Jefferson County house?
sections.html:
Alabama taxes property by class. As published by the Lauderdale County revenue office, Class I is utility property at 30 percent, Class II is all other property at 20 percent, and Class III is agricultural, timber and owner-occupied single-family property at 10 percent.

Appraised value times the class percentage gives assessed value, and the bill is based on assessed value less any exemptions. Because an owner-occupied house sits in the 10 percent class, a rental or second home can carry a heavier assessment than the house next door that is lived in. That difference surprises landlords who sell a Jefferson County rental.

Exemptions generally require an application, and the dollar amounts are set county by county, so confirm yours with the Jefferson County offices before you rely on a number from another county's page.

sections.h2: Who handles Jefferson County property tax questions?
sections.html:
Jefferson County splits the work between a tax assessor, who sets values and hears appeals, and a tax collector, who sends bills and takes payments.

If you do not receive a bill, contact the collector's office. Madison County's published guidance says Alabama law does not require a bill before taxes turn delinquent, so the burden stays with the owner.

The probate court is a separate office. It records the deed after a sale, and it also takes custody of delinquent accounts under the state timetable.

sections.h2: What happens to the tax bill when a Jefferson County house is sold?
sections.html:
The first bill after a sale often shows the previous owner. Lauderdale County explains that the state requires the notice to remain in the name on record the prior October 1, with any exemptions that owner held.

That does not move the responsibility. A buyer owes tax on property they own regardless of whose name is printed on the notice. For sellers, this means two checks at closing:

  • Confirm the current year's tax is paid or prorated.
  • Make sure any delinquent prior-year tax is paid off from the proceeds.
  • Keep a copy of the payoff statement.

Lauderdale's guidance also tells new owners to record the deed, assess the property into their name and claim exemptions before December 31 for purchases made before October 1.

sections.h2: What happens when Jefferson County property tax goes delinquent?
sections.html:
The account moves along the state timetable toward a May sale. Penalties, interest and advertising costs are added along the way, so the amount owed grows each month.

Selling before the sale date is usually the cleaner route. A title company can pay the tax from your proceeds at closing. If the debt is larger than the equity in the house, bring the numbers to the title company early so you know what the closing statement will show.

sections.h2: Does the county's finance history affect homeowners today?
sections.html:
The county declared bankruptcy in 2011 after sewer rates climbed more than 300 percent over 15 years and risky bond swaps led to about $4 billion in debt. Wikipedia describes it as the largest municipal bankruptcy in the country at the time.

The county has limited home rule. It can set zoning, maintain sewers and highways and handle trash disposal, and it can enforce taxation other than property taxes. Property tax rates still come from the statutory process, which is why the same October 1 and December 31 dates apply in Jefferson County as in Lauderdale.

sections.h2: How do roads and rail shape Jefferson County neighborhoods?
sections.html:
Five interstates cross the county: I-20, I-22, I-59, I-65 and I-459, and Wikipedia lists future I-222 and I-422 as well. U.S. Routes 11, 31, 78, 280 and 411 add the older corridors.

Amtrak's Crescent stops in Birmingham, freight rail is run by BNSF, CSX and Norfolk Southern, and Birmingham-Shuttlesworth International Airport handles air service.

sections.h2: What do Jefferson County sellers usually face?
sections.html:
• Estate sales in older Birmingham neighborhoods with several heirs.
  • Rental houses with a higher tax class and deferred repairs.
  • Houses with delinquent tax moving toward the spring sale.
  • Parcels near a county line where the billing office is not obvious.
  • Owners who live out of state and have not seen a bill.

Cash Home Buyers makes written offers on Jefferson County houses in their current condition, with closing run by a local title company that pays unpaid tax from the sale proceeds.

faqs.q: When is Jefferson County, Alabama property tax due?
faqs.a: Property taxes are due October 1 and delinquent after December 31, according to the Alabama Department of Revenue.

faqs.q: What is the Alabama property tax timetable?
faqs.a: The state timetable is October 1 due, January 1 delinquent, February turned over to probate court, March probate court meets, April advertised for sale and May tax sale.

faqs.q: What property classes does Alabama use?
faqs.a: Class I is utilities at 30 percent, Class II is all other property at 20 percent, and Class III is agricultural, timber and owner-occupied single-family property at 10 percent, as published by Lauderdale County.

faqs.q: Why is my Jefferson County tax bill in the previous owner's name?
faqs.a: Alabama keeps the notice in the name on record the previous October 1. The new owner is still responsible for the tax, so confirm it is paid.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Jefferson County house with unpaid property tax?
faqs.a: Yes. The tax is paid from the sale proceeds at closing, and the title company gets the payoff figure from the tax office.

faqs.q: Which county bills my tax if my city is in two counties?
faqs.a: The county where the parcel sits bills it. Birmingham, Hoover, Vestavia Hills, Helena, Leeds and Trussville all reach into another county, so check the parcel record.
